issues.legal_issue: A legislature may provide a reasonable summary procedure for evicting occupants without thereby abridging the constitutional right to property.
material_facts: The challenged law provided a speedier procedure for evicting tenants, sub-tenants, and unauthorised occupants from public premises.
The occupants argued that the summary procedure abridged their property rights.
The Court held that the procedure must be reasonable and conform to the principles of natural justice.
issues.conclusion: Providing a reasonable summary eviction procedure that conforms to natural justice does not, by itself, abridge the constitutional right to property.
issues.legal_principle: Article 19(1)(f), as it stood before its deletion, did not prevent the legislature from prescribing an eviction procedure or withdrawing statutory rent protection. A tenant's interest in premises is property, as recognised in Municipal Corporation of Greater Bombay v. Lala Pancham, but that does not require the legislature to retain a particular eviction procedure or statutory protection. The Public Premises Act creates a speedier remedy for an existing right of eviction rather than a new right of eviction, as explained in Northern India Caterers Private Ltd. v. State of Punjab.

rule.if: eviction_law_challenge and summary_eviction_procedure and procedure_is_reasonable and procedure_observes_natural_justice

predicates.eviction_law_challenge: The proceeding challenges a law that provides for eviction of occupants.
predicates.summary_eviction_procedure: The law provides a summary procedure for evicting occupants.
predicates.procedure_is_reasonable: The procedure prescribed by the law is reasonable.
predicates.procedure_observes_natural_justice: The procedure prescribed by the law conforms to the principles of natural justice.

issues.definition: When a challenged eviction law provides a reasonable summary procedure that observes natural justice, that procedure does not itself abridge the occupants' property right.

issues.legal_issue: Presidential assent to a state law on a concurrent subject overrides only those conflicting central laws whose repugnancy was included in the proposal placed before the President for consideration.
material_facts: The state repeatedly extended the duration of its rent-control law and obtained presidential assent to the extension legislation.
The proposals seeking assent identified repugnancy with specified central laws concerning property transfers and small-cause courts.
The proposals did not identify repugnancy with the central public-premises eviction law.
The High Court examined the correspondence concerning the proposals for assent.
issues.conclusion: The assent did not make the state rent-control law prevail over the central public-premises eviction law, because the proposal for assent did not seek assent in respect of repugnancy with that law.
issues.legal_principle: Article 254(1) gives precedence to a repugnant parliamentary law, subject to Article 254(2). Under Article 254(2), reservation for consideration and assent require the President's attention to be directed to the relevant repugnancy and the reasons for the state law. The assent is limited to the proposal made by the state; where the proposal is confined to specified central laws, it does not extend to other laws. Gram Panchayat of Village Jamalpur v. Malwinder Singh and P.N. Krishan Lal v. Government of Kerala support this approach. Examining the proposal to identify the scope of assent does not amount to reviewing the validity of the President's decision; Hoechst Pharmaceuticals Ltd. v. State of Bihar and Bharat Sevashram Sangh v. State of Gujarat recognise that the assent itself is not justiciable.

predicates.concurrent_law_conflict_case: The proceeding concerns conflicting state and central laws on a concurrent subject.
predicates.state_seeks_presidential_assent: The state submits a proposal seeking presidential assent to its law.
predicates.proposal_identifies_specific_conflicting: The state proposal identifies the central laws whose conflict with the state law is submitted for consideration.
predicates.competing_central_law_not_identified_in_: The central law in dispute is not identified in the proposal seeking assent.

issues.definition: If a state seeking assent identifies particular conflicting central laws but omits the central law later in dispute, the state law does not override that omitted law.

issues.legal_issue: Extending the duration of a temporary enactment without substantially changing its provisions continues the existing enactment rather than enacting a new law.
material_facts: The state legislation extended the duration of a temporary rent-control enactment by changing the date on which it would expire.
The extension legislation did not provide that the rent-control enactment would prevail over the central public-premises eviction law.
The Court distinguished a mere extension from legislation that substantially amends an enactment.
issues.conclusion: An extension of the duration of a temporary enactment, without substantial amendment, is not a new enactment; the existing enactment continues for the extended period.
issues.legal_principle: A temporary enactment whose duration is extended continues as the same law rather than becoming a newly enacted law. The Court relied on State of Bombay v. Heman Santlal Alreja and accepted its reasoning; it distinguished Basantlal Banarsilal v. Bansilal Dagdulal because the legislation there substantially amended the earlier law and involved a distinct source of legislative power. It also considered Kerala State Electricity Board v. Indian Aluminium Co. Ltd. and held that an extension may still require presidential assent where repugnancy makes that necessary.

rule.if: proceeding_concerns_extension_of_temporary_law and temporary_law and extension_changes_duration_only and no_substantial_amendment

predicates.proceeding_concerns_extension_of_tempora: The proceeding concerns the legal effect of legislation extending a temporary law.
predicates.temporary_law: The law whose duration is extended is temporary.
predicates.extension_changes_duration_only: The extension legislation changes the duration of the law without changing its substantive provisions.
predicates.no_substantial_amendment: The extension legislation makes no substantial amendment to the law.

issues.definition: When an extension concerns a temporary law and makes no substantial amendment, the law continues for the extended duration without becoming a new enactment.
